claims.text: As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% terminal strain.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has relatively coarse grains.
Cold rolling followed by recrystallization annealing can convert HfZrTiTa0.53 into a fully recrystallized fine-grained structure with mean grain size below 1 μm.
Fine-grain refinement in HfZrTiTa0.53 will enhance dislocation interactions during deformation.
Fine-grain refinement in HfZrTiTa0.53 will produce a higher density of stacking faults during deformation.
Grain refinement will promote more uniform dislocation motion and accumulation, thereby improving strain hardening.
Improved strain hardening will delay localized necking during tensile deformation.
Delayed necking will increase the tensile uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Solid-solution strengthening in HfZrTiTa0.53 will preserve its yield strength after the treatment.
Solid-solution strengthening and the thermomechanical treatment will preserve impact-triggered chemical energy release.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation from approximately 13.5% to at least approximately 20%.
The treated alloy will maintain yield strength near 786 MPa.
The treated alloy's compressive strength will remain comparable to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy's impact-triggered chemical energy release will remain comparable to the untreated baseline.
The predicted tensile and compressive improvements apply at room temperature under quasi-static loading near 10^-3 s^-1.
The magnitude of ductility improvement depends on rolling reduction and annealing parameters.
Excessive or poorly controlled recrystallization processing may reduce alloy strength.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline is identified as terminal strain in the initial-state and baseline fields, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule treat it as the baseline uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are not interchangeable measurements.
